rule: Each production Worker has ONE canonical code publisher. Every workflow that can change a Worker (code, rollback, secrets or settings) runs inside that Worker's single concurrency group, so changes are serialized. A workflow with a publish command that is not listed here fails tests/publisher-inventory.test.mjs.

zevanory-public-router.t1_unchanged: Single publisher, already in its own group. Left byte-identical so merging T1 does not redeploy the router. Known residual risk (pre-existing): its pull-request runs share the deploy group, so with the default queue a PR run can replace a pending deploy; fix (PR-separated group + queue: max + guard with --tag) in a follow-up the owner schedules.

zevanory-product-control-portable.guard: monotonic guard + authorised rollback in the canonical workflow (#796/#797)

giro-whatsapp-bridge.note: Worker giro-whatsapp-bridge is NOT present in the Cloudflare account (workers list 13/10/2026). whatsapp-broker-protocol-v2.yml patches it via the API and fails reading it (exit 22, run on PR #799); left unchanged and listed under unserialized_known.

rollback_policy: A deliberate rollback is a git revert merged by the owner: a FORWARD promotion whose authorisation trail is the reviewed pull request. promotion_guard.py has no backwards path. Automatic recovery inside a failed release (central wrangler rollback, sales snapshot restore) only returns to the version that was live before that same run; the sales release never deletes the production script.
recovery_when_production_unreadable: Not automatic: the guard refuses. The owner dispatches the canonical workflow after confirming the live version manually (Cloudflare dashboard) or after restoring the readback endpoint; the run is recorded.
credentials: All 19 publishing workflows use the same account-wide tokens (CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN / CLOUDFLARE_PUBLIC_OWNER_API_TOKEN), so credential-level exclusivity does not exist today. Cloudflare supports account-owned API tokens scoped to Specified Workers with the Editor role (changelog 2026-09-15). Target: one token per Worker held only by that Worker's publishers, then revoke the shared tokens. Owner action.
